---
title: "8.7 Limitations and compensating controls"
order: 7
---

The chapter raises six open findings about its own model, rules and gate. Each has evidence
drawn from the facts or the code, a compensating control and an owner. The same six, in the
same words, are D8's open findings in the validation sign-off (D11, in the validation PDF).
The model, the rules and the gate are not changed by this chapter: it documents them as
committed.

Two things are deliberately **not** findings. The model ranks well: it clears its AUC gate,
beats every single input with paired intervals above zero, and gets
{{< var ceiling.li.share_of_reach >}} of the way to the data's ceiling
([8.5](performance.qmd)). And the overlap between the offers and Early Warning's flags,
which a reviewer will see in the customer-360 view, is on this evidence mostly mechanical
and not a sign that the module offers to deteriorating accounts; it is an observation
([below](#li-observations)).

## Finding 1 — The cohort gates cannot fail {#li-finding-1}

**Finding.** `train.py` asserts six gates. Two test the model's ranking on held-out accounts
and one that anything is offered. The other three compare the offered cohort with the book —
lower mean PD, higher mean utilisation, an aggregate incremental ROE at the hurdle — and none
of them can fail: one by construction, two on this book. The gate says nothing about whether
the offers are good.

**Evidence.** From [8.5](performance.qmd#li-headline):

| Gate | Why it cannot fail | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Aggregate incremental ROE ≥ hurdle | by construction: total net income over total allocated equity is an equity-weighted mean of the offers' own ROEs, and every offer's ROE clears the hurdle or it is not an offer | lowest offer ROE {{< var li.cohort_gate.roe.min_offers >}} against {{< var li.gate.roe_hurdle >}}; every offer's allocated equity is the capital ratio times its EAD (asserted in the facts) |
| Cohort mean PD < book mean PD | on this book: the ceiling is the book's median PD, every offer is at or below it, and on this book the median is below the mean | ceiling {{< var li.offer_max_pd >}}, book median {{< var li.cohort_gate.pd.book_median >}}, book mean {{< var li.book_pd >}}: a margin of {{< var li.cohort_gate.pd.margin >}}; highest offer PD {{< var li.cohort_gate.pd.max_offers >}} |
| Cohort mean utilisation > book mean | on this book: an amount needs utilisation above `target_util`, and on this book `target_util` is above the mean | `target_util` {{< var li.config.target_util >}}; utilisation among accounts with an amount: lowest {{< var li.cohort_gate.util.min_amount >}}, median {{< var li.cohort_gate.util.median_amount >}}, mean {{< var li.cohort_gate.util.mean_amount >}}; book mean {{< var li.book_util >}}; only {{< var li.cohort_gate.util.book_share_above_target >}} of the book is above `target_util` |

Every scenario in [8.6](sensitivity.qmd) passes them as well.

**Impact.** The cohort gates read as quality checks and are reported as such in the
validation report and on the portal's summary. They are checks that the rules ran: a
deterioration in what the offers go on to do — more defaults, more deterioration, a lower
label rate — would pass all three. What does measure the cohort is on held-out outcomes
([8.5](performance.qmd#li-cohort)), and nothing gates on it. Neither "cannot fail on this
book" is guaranteed elsewhere: a book whose PD distribution were skewed the other way, or
whose mean utilisation were above `target_util`, could fail them.

**Compensating control.** The headline table states for each gate whether it can fail, and
the facts recompute the evidence on every `verify.py` run. At the next gate review, add cohort
gates that can fail, measured on the held-out offers' outcomes — the observed label rate
against the predicted, deterioration and default not above the book's — with the floor rule
the monitoring plan applies. Until then, read the cohort gates as checks that the rules ran,
never as evidence that the offers are good. The committed gates are not relaxed. **Owner:**
model developer, with the credit policy owner (proposed; to be named).

## Finding 2 — The threshold, the cohort and the served list are in-sample {#li-finding-2}

**Finding.** The model scores the book it was fitted on. The offer threshold is a quantile of
those scores, the offers are chosen from them, and the list the portal serves is their top.
This is the cause behind D7 findings 1 and 2 ([D7.7](../ews/limitations.qmd)), arriving in a
different module.

**Evidence.** The threshold is the {{< var li.config.offer_quantile >}} quantile over all
{{< var li.n_book >}} booked accounts, {{< var li.n_train >}} of them training rows on which
the model's AUC is {{< var li.train.auc >}} ([8.3](methodology.qmd#li-threshold)).
{{< var li.offers.n_train >}} of the {{< var li.n_offered >}} offers are training rows. Their
label rate, {{< var li.offers.rate >}}, compares with {{< var li.offers_ho.observed >}} among
the {{< var li.offers.n_holdout >}} held-out offers. The portal's candidates endpoint serves
the top {{< var li.served.portal.n >}}: {{< var li.served.portal.n_train >}} training rows, all
positive ({{< var li.served.portal.rate >}}); the v1 page's top {{< var li.served.page.n >}}
are {{< var li.served.page.n_train >}} training rows at {{< var li.served.page.rate >}}.

Unlike D7, the effect on the threshold's mechanics is small: on held-out accounts it passes
{{< var li.thr.share_holdout >}}, close to the {{< var li.thr.share_book >}} intended, and the
held-out accounts above it are calibrated within tolerance ([8.5](performance.qmd#li-cohort)).

**Impact.** The visible numbers — the cohort's label rate, the candidates list's perfect hit
rate — overstate what an offer to a new account will achieve. The ranking and the gate are
unaffected; they are held out.

**Compensating control.** Quote the held-out offers' figures only; the facts label every
whole-book figure in-sample. At the next retrain, set the threshold on out-of-fold
probabilities and score the book's training rows out of fold, the retrain control D7 proposes
for the same cause. Until then, read the candidates list as a list to review, never as
evidence of accuracy. **Owner:** model developer, with the portal owner (proposed; to be
named).

## Finding 3 — The lift gate is passed by a single column {#li-finding-3}

**Finding.** The top-quintile lift gate is meant to show that the model concentrates good
candidates at the top. On this data a sort on one column does that too.

**Evidence.** On the held-out accounts ([8.5](performance.qmd#li-baselines)),
{{< var li.baseline.n_pass_lift >}} of the {{< var li.baseline.n_numeric >}} numeric inputs,
each sorted alone, reach the {{< var li.gate.lift_min >}}× gate: utilisation
({{< var li.baseline.utilization.lift >}}×) and revenue ({{< var li.baseline.revenue.lift >}}×)
among them. None reaches the AUC gate; the best single input,
`{{< var li.baseline.best.feature >}}`, reaches {{< var li.baseline.best.auc >}}. The model's
lead over it, {{< var li.baseline.revenue.diff >}}, has a paired interval of
{{< var li.baseline.revenue.diff_lo >}} to {{< var li.baseline.revenue.diff_hi >}}.

**Impact.** The lift gate is redundant with the AUC gate on this data: it would pass a model
no better than a sort on revenue. The model is not weak — it beats every single input — but
one of its two model gates does not show that. The label's observable drivers are inputs by
design ([8.2](data.qmd#li-label)), so this is a property of the gate, not of the model.

**Compensating control.** The facts report the best single input beside both gates on every
run. At the next gate review, restate the lift gate relative to the best single input (for
example, a lift above the best single input's on the same rows). Until then, treat the AUC
gate as the binding test of the model. The committed gate is not changed by this finding.
**Owner:** model developer.

## Finding 4 — A configured hurdle that does nothing {#li-finding-4}

**Finding.** `shared.config.LINE_INCREASE` carries a `roe_hurdle`. No line of the module reads
it; the hurdle that decides every offer is `MARKET`'s.

**Evidence.** A search of `line_increase/src` for every key the code reads from
`LINE_INCREASE` finds all but {{< var li.config.n_unread >}}: `{{< var li.config.unread >}}`.
`incremental_roe` compares with `market.roe_hurdle`, and `train.py`'s aggregate gate with
`MARKET["roe_hurdle"]`:

```python
"clears_hurdle": bool(ead > 0 and w["roe"] >= market.roe_hurdle),       # amount_rules.py
assert agg_incr_roe >= MARKET["roe_hurdle"], (                          # train.py
```

The two values are equal today ({{< var li.config.roe_hurdle >}} and
{{< var li.gate.roe_hurdle >}}).

**Impact.** A credit officer who raises the line-increase hurdle in the module's own
configuration changes nothing, and nothing says so. The hurdle that does act is shared with
pricing, and `MARKET` has no owner or change control beyond code
review (D6 finding 5); a change made for pricing moves the offers too.

**Compensating control.** Remove the key, or pass it to `incremental_roe` as the hurdle, with
a test that a change to it moves the offers. Until then, change the hurdle only in `MARKET`, under
D6's control, and re-run [8.5](performance.qmd) after any change; the facts list every unread
key of `LINE_INCREASE` on each `verify.py` run. **Owner:** model developer.

## Finding 5 — The exposure rests on an unvalidated drawdown {#li-finding-5}

**Finding.** Every exposure figure the module reports assumes that an increase is drawn at the
account's current utilisation. Nothing supports that, and the limit the bank commits is
larger.

**Evidence.** From [8.4](assumptions.qmd#li-drawdown) and
[8.5](performance.qmd#li-economics): the {{< var li.n_offered >}} offers commit
\${{< var li.econ.amount_total >}}; the reported incremental exposure is
\${{< var li.econ.exposure_total >}}. The ROE of each offer does not depend on the drawdown;
the aggregate does, a little: {{< var li.econ.full_draw.agg_roe >}} if every increase were
fully drawn, against {{< var li.agg_roe >}}, with the same
{{< var li.econ.full_draw.n_offered >}} offers. The data hold no drawdown to measure.

**Impact.** Who is offered does not change. What the offers add to the bank's exposure,
capital and income does: a business near its limit may well draw more of new room than its
current share, and an undrawn limit is still a commitment. The portal's segments show only the
assumed exposure.

**Compensating control.** Report the committed amount beside the assumed exposure (the facts
and the economics table do). Size limits and capital on the committed amount, never on the
assumed exposure. Before any real use, measure drawdown on granted increases and replace the
assumption. **Owner:** model developer, with the portfolio owner (proposed; to be named).

## Finding 6 — The label is constructed, not observed {#li-finding-6}

**Finding.** `{{< var li.target >}}` is drawn by the generator for every booked account. No
increase was offered or granted, so the label is not the outcome of one, and what "good" means
has no definition outside the generator's code.

**Evidence.** The generator draws the label from the true PD, utilisation above a level,
revenue and later deterioration, with noise ([8.2](data.qmd#li-label)). The data record no
offer, take-up, drawdown or repayment. The ceiling in [8.5](performance.qmd#li-ceiling) is the
ceiling for ranking that construction.

**Impact.** Every performance figure in this chapter measures how well the model recovers the
generator's construction. On a real book the outcome of an increase is observed only for
accounts that were given one, chosen by whatever policy chose them; a model trained on those
alone learns that policy as well as the outcome. This is a property of the synthetic data, not
a defect in the code, but it goes to what the model is for, so it is a finding, as D7's lead
time is.

**Compensating control.** Before any real use, define the label as an observed outcome of an
increase over a stated window — for example, the increase taken up and the account performing
over the following year — and plan for selection, for instance by offering to a randomised
hold-out. Until then, make no claim about how offered accounts would perform (a prohibited
use, [8.1](purpose.qmd#prohibited-uses)). **Owner:** model developer, with the credit policy
owner (proposed; to be named).
